title: Constraint Graph-based PCB Legalization Considering Dense, Heterogeneous, Irregular-Shaped, and Any-oriented Components
problem: Modern PCB designs with dense, heterogeneous, irregular-shaped, and any-oriented components pose challenges for automatic placement legalization, especially double-sided designs. Existing methods rely on naive bounding box approximations and cannot handle complex constraints effectively.
motivation: PCB design automation is increasingly complex; effective legalization that handles non-rectangular components and orientation constraints is essential for high-density, multi-layer board designs.
method: First constraint graph-based legalization approach for PCBs. Uses slicing technique to model components accurately via rectangles instead of bounding box approximation. Employs Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) formulation to expand solution space for heterogeneous, irregular-shaped, any-oriented components in high-density designs.
key_novelty: First constraint graph-based legalization with accurate slicing-based component modeling and MILP formulation for complex heterogeneous, irregular PCB components.
contributions: First constraint graph-based PCB legalization method
Accurate component modeling via slicing (rectangles vs. bounding boxes)
MILP formulation for heterogeneous and any-oriented components
Support for high-density double-sided PCB designs

metrics.other: Legalization success, design robustness (specific metrics not provided)

limitations: Specific quantitative comparisons and computational complexity analysis not detailed; scalability to extremely large boards not discussed.
primary_theme: Constraint graph-based PCB legalization for complex heterogeneous components
